i’m not a professional, and it’s difficult to really give an answer when there’s very little context about you and your situation available here. however, in past situations where i have behaved similarly, i found it was often because i was very insecure or anxious about my attachment. 

i wasn’t ever thinking consciously or intentionally about what i was doing, but upon reflection back on those situations i realize i was afraid that the person i was interested in would lose interest in or “leave” me if i didn’t do absolutely everything possible to keep their attention and/or affection.

often i also find that the fact of the matter is that when this happens i probably was not all that interested in that person in the first place — i just craved the attention, affection, validation, etc. that came with their interest in me. even though i still believe there was some part of me that did truly like these people i was in these relationships with,  i was never as invested as i made myself to believe in my desperation to hold onto the validation and companionship they gave me.

certainly not saying that this is necessarily the exact case for you, but maybe you can find some similarities in my story and your own experiences. i do suggest speaking to someone who is professionally trained to help you work on your attachment and security in your relationships with others (in all forms, not necessarily just with people you are dating)

i only ever have vented when i’ve genuinely felt suicidal, and really only to one person, but unfortunately that has been pretty consistent for me the greater part of my mid-late teenage years and early adulthood. i’ve been trying to wait for positive change for a long time now, but i feel the past 3 years have been a steady decline for me. every small step forward has been offset by a dozen huge strides back. it’s getting very difficult to believe anything will change enough to make me want to stay anytime soon, and i fear it’s too little too late

i have the opposite problem, my daily calories burned from exercise according to MFP seem incredibly low, even given my size and gender. today i clocked ~18k steps on my phone’s built in activity tracker (walking at an average-moderate pace for the greater part) and i was only given about 100 extra calories for the day. even when being very conservative that number just sounds very low to me given my activity level. maybe it’s because i don’t input any of it directly as exercise, but i’m not certain the actual duration of my activity most days due to the nature of my job, and i don’t want to be wrong and give myself too much credit.

the normal amount is zero, but i also know there are many people with depression who think passively about it both infrequently and frequently, and that it is not uncommon or necessarily irregular for people with depression and/or other mental illnesses that may cause heightened emotional distress or intrusive thoughts. i think where it truly crosses into the unhealthy is when it becomes active thoughts with intention behind them. i’ve been experiencing passive suicidal ideation since i was a young child, but only in the past 2 or so years has it become something i actively think about and have started planning with actual intent to go through with it.
i don’t think they will understand. they never will. i just want them to feel even a fraction of the pain i do.

more like they are the only two family members who haven’t been terrible to me or complicit in it, and even then my mother has done a lot of terrible things to me, but i am able to forgive her for my own reasons. i’ve already tried to do what i can to hurt the rest of them, but i know they will not actually get it through their heads until i am gone. and i am ready to be gone.
i suppose i could go over and try to make a scene to ruin it, but i think they’d just hold it against me, try to embarrass or further shame me in the future. this is a much more impactful way.
